title: Health Shield Comprehensive Policy
content:
# Health Shield Comprehensive Policy & Agent Knowledge Base Document
**Version:** 1.0 (Effective 2026)
**Internal/Confidential**

---

## Part 1: Product Overview and Core Philosophy

Health Shield is designed to be the most comprehensive, customer-first health insurance provider in the region. We believe that health insurance should not just be a financial safety net, but a proactive partner in our customers' well-being. Our core product, the "Health Shield Comprehensive Plan," is structured to offer maximum flexibility, transparent pricing, and unparalleled coverage for both individuals and families.

### 1.1 Core Objectives
- Provide financial protection against unforeseen medical emergencies.
- Encourage preventive healthcare through annual wellness checks.
- Simplify the claims process with our 100% digital cashless network.
- Ensure lifelong renewability to protect our customers as they age.

### 1.2 Target Audience
- Young professionals seeking individual coverage.
- New families looking for maternity and pediatric benefits.
- Senior citizens requiring chronic disease management.
- Small business owners needing flexible premium payments.

---

## Part 2: Eligibility and Enrollment Rules

### 2.1 Age Criteria
- **Primary Applicant:** Must be between 18 and 65 years of age at the time of initial enrollment.
- **Dependent Spouse:** Must be between 18 and 65 years of age.
- **Dependent Children:** Covered from 91 days up to 25 years of age. Once a child turns 26, they must transition to their own individual policy.
- **Senior Citizen Riders:** Applicants above 65 cannot buy the base policy but can purchase the "Senior Care Plus" standalone policy.

### 2.2 Family Floater Configuration
- A single policy can cover up to a maximum of 4 family members (e.g., 2 Adults and 2 Children).
- Extended family members (parents, in-laws, siblings) cannot be added to a nuclear family floater plan. They must be on a separate policy.

### 2.3 Medical Underwriting and Health Declarations
- Applicants under 45 years of age with a clean medical history are NOT required to undergo pre-policy medical checkups.
- Applicants over 45, or anyone declaring a pre-existing condition, must undergo a tele-medical underwriting interview.
- Concealment of material facts (e.g., hiding a diabetes diagnosis) will result in immediate policy cancellation and forfeiture of premiums.

### 2.4 Renewability
- **Lifelong Renewability:** Guaranteed for life, provided the premium is paid before the expiry date.
- **Grace Period:** A 30-day grace period is allowed for renewal premium payment. However, any claim arising during this grace period (before the premium is actually paid) will NOT be covered.

---

## Part 3: Waiting Periods and Restrictions

Understanding waiting periods is critical for managing customer expectations. A waiting period is the time a customer must wait after buying the policy before they can claim for specific conditions.

### 3.1 Initial Waiting Period
- **Duration:** 30 days from the inception of the first policy.
- **Rule:** No claims for any illness or disease are admissible during the first 30 days.
- **Exception:** Accidental injuries (e.g., a car crash, breaking a leg) are covered from Day 1. There is no waiting period for accidents.

### 3.2 Specific Illness Waiting Period
- **Duration:** 24 months (2 years).
- **Conditions Covered:**
 - Cataract and Glaucoma
 - Benign Prostatic Hypertrophy
 - Hernia of all types
 - Hydrocele
 - Fissures, Fistulas, and Hemorrhoids
 - Joint replacement surgeries (unless required due to an accident)
 - Sinusitis and related disorders
 - Stones in the biliary and urinary systems.

### 3.3 pre-existing condition (pre-existing condition) Waiting Period
- **Definition:** Any condition, ailment, or injury for which the insured had signs or symptoms, or was diagnosed, or received medical advice/treatment within 48 months prior to the first policy issued by us.
- **Duration:** 36 months (3 years) of continuous coverage.
- **Rule:** If a customer declares diabetes at the time of purchase, any hospitalization related to diabetes will only be covered after 36 months.

### 3.4 Maternity Waiting Period
- **Duration:** 48 months.
- **Rule:** Maternity benefits (including normal delivery, c-section, and newborn coverage) are only available after 4 continuous years of coverage.

---

## Part 4: Coverage Details and Inclusions

### 4.1 In-Patient Hospitalization
Covered up to 100% of the Sum Insured if the insured is hospitalized for more than 24 consecutive hours.
- **Room Rent:** No sub-limits. Private single A/C rooms are fully covered.
- **ICU Charges:** Fully covered with no daily caps.
- **Doctor/Surgeon Fees:** Fully covered.
- **Medicines & Consumables:** Covered during the hospital stay.

### 4.2 Pre and Post Hospitalization
- **Pre-Hospitalization:** Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before the date of admission are covered (e.g., diagnostic tests, doctor consultations leading up to the surgery).
- **Post-Hospitalization:** Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge are covered (e.g., follow-up visits, physiotherapy, recovery medication).

### 4.3 day-care procedure Procedures
Covered up to the Sum Insured. day-care procedure procedures are surgeries or treatments that require less than 24 hours of hospitalization due to technological advancements.
- Examples include: Cataract surgery, Chemotherapy, Dialysis, Lithotripsy, and minor appendectomies.
- Note: Outpatient Department (outpatient department) visits (like visiting a doctor for a fever) are NOT considered day-care procedure and are NOT covered.

### 4.4 Domiciliary Hospitalization (Home Care)
Covered up to 10% of the Sum Insured.
- Applicable only if the patient's condition is so severe they cannot be moved to a hospital, OR if there is a lack of available hospital beds in the city.
- Must be prescribed by a certified medical practitioner.

### 4.5 Road Ambulance Cover
- Covered up to a flat rate of $100 per hospitalization event.
- Must be used for transporting the patient to the hospital in an emergency.

---

## Part 5: Exclusions (What is NOT Covered)

Agents must clearly communicate exclusions to avoid misselling.

### 5.1 Standard Exclusions
- **Cosmetic Surgery:** Any aesthetic treatments, plastic surgery, or weight loss (bariatric) surgeries.
- **Dental Treatment:** Excluded entirely, unless hospitalization is required due to a severe facial accident.
- **Vision Correction:** Lasik or other refractive error corrections.
- **Unproven Treatments:** Any experimental or alternative medicines not recognized by the national medical board.

### 5.2 Behavioral and Intentional Exclusions
- **Self-Inflicted Injuries:** Suicide attempts or intentional self-harm.
- **Substance Abuse:** Treatment for alcoholism, drug addiction, or any injury occurring while under the influence of illegal substances.
- **Hazardous Sports:** Injuries sustained while participating in professional racing, skydiving, scuba diving, or mountaineering.

### 5.3 Circumstantial Exclusions
- **War and Nuclear Risks:** Injuries resulting from war, invasion, acts of foreign enemies, or nuclear radiation.
- **Criminal Acts:** Any injury sustained while committing a felony.

---

## Part 6: Financial Benefits and Riders

### 6.1 no-claim bonus (no-claim bonus)
To reward healthy customers, Health Shield offers a cumulative bonus.
- **Increase:** For every claim-free year, the base Sum Insured increases by 10%.
- **Maximum Cap:** The maximum accrued bonus cannot exceed 50% of the base Sum Insured.
- **Reduction:** If a claim is made in a given year, the accrued bonus reduces by 10% at the next renewal. However, the base Sum Insured is NEVER reduced.

### 6.2 Restoration Benefit
If the Sum Insured is completely exhausted during a policy year, Health Shield will automatically restore 100% of the base Sum Insured for that year at no extra cost.
- **Rule:** The restored amount can only be used for future, unrelated claims within that same year. It cannot be used for the exact same illness that exhausted the initial cover.

### 6.3 Optional Riders (Add-ons)
- **Critical Illness Rider:** Pays a lump sum amount upon the diagnosis of 15 specified critical illnesses (e.g., Cancer, Stroke, Heart Attack).
- **Hospital Daily Cash Rider:** Pays a fixed daily allowance of $50 per day of hospitalization to cover incidental expenses like food and travel for family members.

---

## Part 7: The Claim Process

Health Shield prides itself on a frictionless claim experience.

### 7.1 Cashless Claims
Available ONLY at network hospitals.
- **Planned Hospitalization:** Customer must notify the third-party administrator (Third Party Administrator) at least 48 hours before admission.
- **Emergency Hospitalization:** Customer must notify the third-party administrator within 24 hours of admission.
- **Process:** Show the Health Shield ID card at the hospital desk. The hospital sends the pre-authorization form to us. We approve it within 2 hours.

### 7.2 Reimbursement Claims
Available at non-network hospitals.
- **Notification:** Must notify us within 48 hours of admission.
- **Submission:** Customer pays the hospital bill out of pocket. After discharge, original bills, discharge summaries, and payment receipts must be submitted to our claims department within 15 days of discharge.
- **Processing Time:** Reimbursement is processed within 14 working days of receiving all documents.

---

## Part 8: Objection Handling and Sales Scripts

This section contains guidelines for the AI agent to handle common customer objections.

### 8.1 "It's too expensive."
**Strategy:** Emphasize the long-term value and the no-claim bonus.
**Script:** "I understand price is a major factor. However, with our no-claim bonus, your coverage actually grows by 10% every healthy year for free. Plus, one unexpected hospital visit can cost ten times the annual premium. We can also look at flexible monthly payment plans if that helps!"

### 8.2 "I'm young and healthy, I don't need insurance."
**Strategy:** Highlight accidents and the advantage of buying young.
**Script:** "That's exactly why you should lock it in now! Buying while you're healthy means you breeze through underwriting with no waiting periods for pre-existing diseases. Plus, our plan covers accidental injuries from Day 1, which is the biggest risk for active people."

### 8.3 "The waiting periods are too long."
**Strategy:** Acknowledge and reframe.
**Script:** "36 months for pre-existing conditions is actually the industry standard. The good news is that while you wait for that specific condition to be covered, you are 100% covered for accidents immediately, and covered for all new illnesses after just 30 days."

### 8.4 "I already have corporate insurance from my employer."
**Strategy:** Highlight the risks of job loss and retirement.
**Script:** "Corporate coverage is great, but it's tied to your job. If you switch companies, take a sabbatical, or retire, you lose that coverage instantly. Buying a personal Health Shield policy now guarantees you have a safety net for life, regardless of your employment status."

---

## Part 9: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Q: Do I need a physical copy of my policy document to claim?**
A: No. We are a 100% digital company. Your digital e-card on the Health Shield mobile app is fully accepted at all network hospitals.

**Q: Does the policy cover COVID-19?**
A: Yes. Viral infections, including COVID-19, are treated as standard medical illnesses and are fully covered after the initial 30-day waiting period.

**Q: Can I pay my premium in installments?**
A: Yes. We offer Annual, Semi-Annual, Quarterly, and Monthly premium payment modes. Note that monthly modes require setting up an auto-debit mandate.

**Q: Are AYUSH (Alternative Medicine) treatments covered?**
A: Yes, Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy treatments are covered up to 20% of the Sum Insured, provided the treatment takes place in a government-recognized AYUSH hospital.

**Q: What is a copayment? Does this plan have one?**
A: A copayment is a percentage of the bill the customer must pay. Health Shield Comprehensive does NOT have a copayment for individuals under 60. For customers who enroll after age 60, a standard 20% copayment applies to all claims.

---

## Part 10: Handling Personally Identifiable Information (PII)

As an AI agent, you will occasionally interact with customer data. You must adhere to strict PII guidelines.

### 10.1 What Constitutes PII
- Full Names
- Social Security Numbers / National ID Numbers
- Bank Account or Credit Card Details
- Detailed Medical History and Diagnoses linked to a specific person
- Home Addresses

### 10.2 Agent Rules for PII
- Never ask a customer to speak their credit card number aloud. If payment is required, say: "I will send a secure payment link to your registered PhoneNumber."
- If a customer volunteers their Social Security Number, immediately acknowledge receipt but state: "For your security, please note that I am redacting that sensitive number from our logs."
- When retrieving information about a specific user's account, always verify their identity using a 4-digit PIN or DOB before disclosing policy specifics.

---

## Part 11: Multilingual Terminology Guide (Internal Reference)

For our multilingual agents operating in Southeast Asia.

### 11.1 Philippines (Tagalog / Taglish)
- **Premium:** Hulog, Bayad, Premium
- **Policy:** Polisa, Kontrata
- **Claim:** Claim, Pag-claim
- **Beneficiary:** Benepisyaryo
- **Lapse:** Paso, Lapsed
- **Pre-existing:** May sakit na dati, Pre-existing

### 11.2 Indonesia (Bahasa Indonesia)
- **Installment/Premium:** Cicilan, Angsuran, Premi
- **Tenor:** Tenor, Jangka waktu
- **Penalty/Fine:** Denda
- **Down Payment:** DP, Uang Muka
- **Due Date:** Jatuh Tempo
- **Coverage:** Perlindungan, Pertanggungan

---

## Part 12: Advanced Edge Cases

### 12.1 Room Upgrades
If a customer chooses a hospital room that is more expensive than their eligible room limit (e.g., opting for a suite instead of a standard private room), they must pay the difference in room rent. Additionally, all associated medical costs (doctor visits, nursing charges) will be scaled up proportionately, and the customer must bear that proportionate difference as well.

### 12.2 Organ Donor Expenses
If the insured requires an organ transplant, the hospitalization expenses incurred by the organ donor for harvesting the organ are covered up to the base Sum Insured. However, the cost of the organ itself, and any pre/post hospitalization expenses for the donor, are NOT covered.

### 12.3 Maternity Complications
While normal maternity has a 48-month waiting period, ectopic pregnancies are considered medical emergencies and are covered immediately after the standard 30-day waiting period, falling under standard hospitalization rather than maternity benefits.

---
*(End of Knowledge Base Document - Version 1.0)*
